# Feature: Browser Widget Drivers

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-FP-010
**Source**: Plan Feature agent (self-contained — no plan file)
**Predecessor**: FEAT-FP-009 (`feature_browser_widget_observability.md`) — implemented, and the
reason this feature exists: it proved that enriching the observation is the wrong layer for this
class of problem.

Give the agent **semantic tools for stateful UI widgets** — dates, and choose-from-offered-choices
controls — so it stops reverse-engineering interaction protocols out of a flat element list. The
model states _what_ it wants; a deterministic driver in `packages/core` works out _how_, verifies
the result against the widget's own committed state, and returns either a verified success or a
typed failure carrying what it actually observed.

### Why the previous approach did not work

FEAT-FP-009 landed correctly — day cells are now named `"1"`, `"2"`, `"3"` and carry
`disabled: true`. The run got **worse**: `20260807T031509Z-do-a2b06a08` took **76 tool calls,
628s**, with 8× `FORM_WIDGET_NO_MATCH`, 2× `SUGGESTION_NOT_OFFERED`, 6× `URL_NOT_FROM_EVIDENCE`,
against 67 calls / 459s for the pre-fix baseline. Richer observations made the model try _harder
by hand_ while the tool path stayed broken.

The structural reason: **a widget is a stateful protocol, not a set of elements.** Its
intermediate states are only meaningful inside the interaction loop. Exposing the elements and
asking the model to sequence them means every probe costs a full round trip (~8s, ~1k tokens),
and the model cannot verify an outcome without spending another one. A driver's probe costs
~200ms and no tokens, so it can afford to open, read, page, cross-check, retry, and back out —
and it can read signal that has no business in the model's context: `datetime`/`data-date`
attributes, `<table>` structure, `<th>` weekday headers, `aria-controls` targets, and
before/after DOM diffs.

The decisive mechanism is the **weekday cross-check**: derive each calendar cell's date from its
table position plus the panel's month label, then verify the derived weekday matches the column
the cell sits in. Disagreement means the mapping is wrong — refuse instead of clicking. That check
would have caught _"clicked what I thought was Aug 6, got Sep 5"_ in 200ms rather than eight model
turns. The model has no way to run it.

### Confirmed faults this feature retires

| #   | Fault                                                                                         | Evidence                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| --- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A   | `pickSuggestion` filters `entry.role === 'option'`                                            | `browser-form-fill.ts:290`. Expedia's suggestions are `role: "button"`, so the 3s wait always times out. The very next `browser_observe` shows `{"ref":"e76","role":"button","name":"Frisco Texas, United States"}` sitting there. 2× `SUGGESTION_NOT_OFFERED`.     |
| B   | `computeGroup` returns `null` on the first matching ancestor instead of continuing the walk   | `interactable-scan.ts:184` — `return heading?.trim() ? … : null` sits inside the match branch. Expedia's day cell hits the inner `<table>` first; no caption, no heading → `null`, never reaching the panel holding "August 2026". Every day cell lost its `group`. |
| C   | With `group` null, the day-cell tier correctly refuses to guess between two cells named `"6"` | 8× `FORM_WIDGET_NO_MATCH`, each listing page chrome (`"Skip to main content"`, `"Communication Center"`, …) as the "visible choices".                                                                                                                               |
| D   | `chooseInWidget` clicks the trigger unconditionally, closing a widget the site already opened | Expedia auto-opens the date picker after a destination is chosen. The first `browser_form_fill` field then _closes_ it, and the follow-up observation finds 71 page elements and no calendar.                                                                       |
| E   | `(top, left)` ordering cannot de-interleave side-by-side month panels                         | They genuinely share rows. Observed: `e89`="1"(disabled, Aug 1), `e90`="1"(Sep 1), `e91`–`e94`="2".."5"(Sep), `e95`="2"(disabled, Aug 2)… De-interleaving needs _panel-major_ ordering, which needs `group` (fault B).                                              |

**Target**: the Expedia goal completes with correct dates in ≲12 tool calls, with zero
`FORM_WIDGET_NO_MATCH` and zero `SUGGESTION_NOT_OFFERED`.

## 2. Technical Context

### Approach

**One driver layer, three call sites.** All widget logic lives in `packages/core/src/widgets/`
behind a `WidgetDriver` contract. `browser_pick_date`, `browser_pick_option`, and
`browser_form_fill` are thin adapters over the same registry — there is no second implementation
to drift. `browser_form_fill` keeps its full-form role and auto-dispatches each field through
`registry.detect()`; the dedicated tools name their driver family explicitly and skip detection.

**Drivers are pattern-based, never site-based.** `native-select`, `listbox`, `typeahead`,
`calendar-grid`, `date-input`. No driver may reference a hostname, a `data-testid` value specific
to one vendor, or a class name. A pattern that only one site uses does not belong here.

**Detection is cheap, closed-state, and only matters for auto-dispatch.** `detect()` reads the
trigger's tag, role, `type`, `aria-haspopup`, `aria-autocomplete`, the _shape_ of its
`aria-controls`/`aria-owns` target, and — a signal FEAT-FP-009 already gave us for free — its
**committed value**: a trigger reading `"Dates, Thu, Aug 6 - Fri, Aug 7"` parses as a date range
and scores the calendar driver highly without opening anything. Detection never opens a widget and
never clicks. When `browser_pick_date` is called explicitly, a wrong detection cannot hurt it —
the tool asserts the family.

**Open-state is checked, never assumed.** Fault D exists because `chooseInWidget` clicks to open
unconditionally. `open-state.ts` resolves the trigger's controlled container
(`aria-controls` → `aria-owns` → `aria-haspopup` sibling popup → a container that appeared in a
before/after DOM diff) and reports open/closed from `aria-expanded` plus the container's
visibility. A driver opens only when closed, and restores the prior state on exit so the next
field in a `browser_form_fill` batch is not toggled shut.

**Never report unverified success.** Every driver ends by re-reading the trigger's committed value
through `verify.ts` and comparing it to the intent. A mismatch, an ambiguous choice, or a failed
weekday cross-check is a typed retryable failure carrying the observed state — never a click on a
guess. This is the property that makes the tool trustworthy enough for the model to stop
second-guessing it, and it is why "strict, then heuristic fallback" was rejected: name matching is
exactly what produced "Sep 5" for "Aug 6" and reported it as success.

**Ref resolution.** Drivers read structure in-page but must act through
`AgentBrowserController.click()`/`fill()` to keep the settle, navigation, popup, and dialog
semantics. Primary strategy: match the in-page structural read back to a ref from a fresh uncapped
`observe({ cap: 400 })` by `(name, group)`. Fallback when `group` is unavailable: tag the target
in-page with a unique `data-yantra-widget-target` attribute, resolve it to a handle, and **remove
the attribute in a `finally`** — a driver call must leave no Yantra attribute on the page.

**Trace stays primitive.** Drivers append the same `click`/`fill` trace steps they actually
perform, so `AgentTrace`, `promoteAgentTrace`, the workflow YAML schema, and every saved workflow
are untouched. A promoted calendar chain remains as date-brittle as it is today — no better, no
worse. Semantic step kinds are filed in `TODO.md`.

### Spec-Specific Overrides

- **No system-prompt change and no `PROMPT_VERSION` bump.** All guidance goes into tool
  descriptions (the model's primary affordance) and the `do` profile addendum, both of which are
  per-run text. `AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT` stays at `agent-v7` from FEAT-FP-009 so persisted prompt
  hashes remain comparable across this change.
- **Drivers live in `core` and must not import `@yantra/agent`** (memory §Project Structure). The
  `WidgetPort` interface in `widgets/types.ts` is the seam; `AgentBrowserController` implements it.
- No other overrides — see `.spec-lite/memory.md`.

## 3. Data Model (Granular)

No persistent schema changes; no workflow YAML change; no protocol change. New in-memory contracts:

### Entities & Attributes

- **`WidgetPort`** (`widgets/types.ts`) — the narrow seam drivers act through, implemented by `AgentBrowserController`:
  - `observe(options)` → `AgentBrowserObservation` (uncapped, internal)
  - `click(ref)` / `fill(ref, value)` → the controller's settle-aware actions
  - `evaluateOn<T>(ref, fn, ...args)` → in-page read against a resolved element
  - `evaluate<T>(fn, ...args)` → in-page read against the document
  - `now()` → injectable clock for bounded waits

- **`WidgetTarget`**:
  - `ref` (string) — the trigger/field element
  - `role` (string), `name` (string), `group` (string | null), `value` (string | null) — from the observation

- **`WidgetIntent`** — discriminated union:
  - `{ kind: 'date', date: string }` — ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`
  - `{ kind: 'date_range', from: string, to: string }`
  - `{ kind: 'option', value: string }`

- **`WidgetOutcome`** — discriminated union:
  - `{ ok: true, driver: string, committed: string, actions: number }` — `committed` is the trigger's verified rendered value
  - `{ ok: false, errorCode: WidgetErrorCode, message: string, retryable: boolean, details: Record<string, unknown> }`

- **`WidgetErrorCode`** — closed set:
  - `WIDGET_NOT_RECOGNIZED` — no driver reached the confidence threshold
  - `WIDGET_DID_NOT_OPEN` — trigger clicked, no container became visible within the bound
  - `WIDGET_TARGET_UNREACHABLE` — the requested date/option is not offered and paging is exhausted
  - `WIDGET_AMBIGUOUS_CHOICE` — two or more candidates tie; `details.offered` lists them
  - `WIDGET_MAPPING_UNSAFE` — the weekday cross-check failed; `details.derived`/`details.column`
  - `WIDGET_NOT_COMMITTED` — the click landed but the trigger's value does not reflect the intent; `details.committed`

- **`WidgetDriver`**:
  - `kind` (string), `family` (`'date' | 'option'`)
  - `detect(port, target)` → `number` confidence in `[0, 1]`; must not open or click
  - `drive(port, target, intent, budget)` → `WidgetOutcome`

- **`WidgetBudget`**: `deadlineMs` (absolute), `maxPagingSteps` (default 12), `maxActions` (default 24)

### Relationships

- One `WidgetRegistry` holds N `WidgetDriver`, tried in registration order; the highest confidence
  ≥ `MIN_CONFIDENCE` (0.5) wins, ties broken by registration order.
- One `browser_form_fill` call dispatches N fields, each to at most one driver.

### Indexes & Constraints

- `MIN_CONFIDENCE = 0.5`. A registry with no driver above it returns `WIDGET_NOT_RECOGNIZED`
  rather than picking the best of a bad set.
- Every driver is bounded by `WidgetBudget`; exceeding it is `WIDGET_TARGET_UNREACHABLE`, never a
  hang.

## 6. Implementation Tasks

### TASK-001: Widget driver contract, registry, open-state, and verification

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - Create `widgets/types.ts` with every contract in §3. `WidgetErrorCode` is a closed union — no
    string escape hatch.
  - Create `widgets/registry.ts`: `registerDriver`, `detectDriver(port, target, family?)` returning
    the highest-confidence driver ≥ `MIN_CONFIDENCE` (0.5, ties by registration order), and
    `driveWidget(port, target, intent, budget)` which dispatches and returns the driver's outcome.
    A `family` argument restricts the search — that is how the dedicated tools skip detection.
  - Create `widgets/open-state.ts`:
    - `resolveContainer(port, target)` — in order: `aria-controls` id, `aria-owns` id, an
      `aria-haspopup` trigger's next visible popup sibling, then a **before/after DOM diff**
      (snapshot the set of visible container elements, click, re-snapshot, take the newly visible
      one). Returns an opaque container descriptor or `null`.
    - `isOpen(port, target, container)` — `aria-expanded === 'true'` when present, else the
      container's visibility (non-zero box, not `display:none`/`visibility:hidden`).
    - `openIfClosed(port, target)` — no-op when already open; otherwise click the trigger and poll
      for the container up to `OPEN_WAIT_MS = 3000` at `POLL_MS = 100`. Returns
      `{ container, wasOpen }`, or `WIDGET_DID_NOT_OPEN`.
    - `restore(port, target, wasOpen)` — closes the widget when it was closed on entry, preferring
      `Escape` over a second trigger click (a second click re-opens some widgets).
  - Create `widgets/verify.ts`: `readCommitted(port, target)` returns the trigger's current
    `value ?? accessible name`; `matchesIntent(committed, intent)` parses dates out of a rendered
    string (locale-tolerant via `Intl`) for date intents and does normalized containment for option
    intents.
  - Create `widgets/tagging.ts`: `withTag(port, inPageSelectorFn, body)` sets
    `data-yantra-widget-target` on the resolved element, runs `body` with the resolved ref, and
    removes the attribute in a `finally` — including on throw.
  - Implement `WidgetPort` on `AgentBrowserController` (add `evaluate`/`evaluateOn`; the rest
    already exist). Export the barrel from `packages/core/src/index.ts`.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**:
  - Registry picks the highest confidence; ties resolve by registration order.
  - No driver ≥ 0.5 → `WIDGET_NOT_RECOGNIZED`, and **no driver's `drive` was called**.
  - `family: 'date'` restricts detection to date drivers even when an option driver scores higher.
  - `detect()` implementations are asserted not to call `port.click` or `port.fill` (spy port).
  - `openIfClosed` on an already-open widget performs **zero** clicks and reports `wasOpen: true` —
    the direct regression test for fault D.
  - `openIfClosed` on a closed widget that never opens → `WIDGET_DID_NOT_OPEN` after the bound,
    with no unbounded wait.
  - `restore` closes a widget that was closed on entry and leaves an already-open one alone.
  - `withTag` removes the attribute on the success path **and** when `body` throws.
  - `matchesIntent('Thu, Sep 6 - Sat, Sep 8', {kind:'date_range',from:'2026-09-06',to:'2026-09-08'})`
    → true; `'Sep 3 - Sep 4'` → false.

### TASK-002: Option drivers — native select, listbox, and typeahead

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - `native-select-driver.ts` — `detect` returns 1.0 for `<select>`; `drive` reuses the controller's
    existing `fillSelect` semantics (value or label match, `input`+`change` dispatch) and verifies
    via `readCommitted`.
  - `listbox-driver.ts` — for a trigger whose container is a `[role="listbox"]`, `[role="menu"]`,
    or a popup holding a homogeneous set of clickable children. `drive`: `openIfClosed`, collect
    candidates, rank, click, verify, `restore`.
  - `typeahead-driver.ts` — `detect` scores on `aria-autocomplete`, `role="combobox"` with a text
    input, or a textbox with `aria-controls`/`aria-owns`. `drive`: focus, clear, type the value
    through `port.fill`, then poll up to `SUGGESTION_WAIT_MS = 3000` at 150ms for candidates.
  - **Candidate collection must not require `role="option"`** — this is fault A. Accept any
    clickable descendant of the resolved container: `[role="option"]`, `button`, `a[href]`,
    `[role="menuitem"]`, `li` with a click handler, or any element with a non-empty accessible
    name inside a container that has ≥2 such siblings. Rank by name match against the requested
    value: exact (case/whitespace-normalized) → prefix → all-tokens-present → substring.
  - **Ambiguity is a failure, not a coin flip**: when the best and runner-up land in the same tier,
    return `WIDGET_AMBIGUOUS_CHOICE` with `details.offered` listing up to 10 candidate names.
  - Verify the field **committed**: after the click, `readCommitted` must contain the chosen
    candidate's text, or at minimum differ from the raw typed text. Otherwise
    `WIDGET_NOT_COMMITTED` with `details.committed`.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**:
  - jsdom fixture reproducing Expedia's shape — a textbox plus a container of `role="button"`
    children named `"Frisco Texas, United States"`, `"Toyota Stadium Frisco, Texas, United States"`,
    … — resolves to the first for value `"Frisco, Texas"`. **This is the fault-A regression test.**
  - A container of `role="option"` children still works (no regression).
  - Native `<select>` selects by visible label and by value.
  - Suggestions that arrive after 1.2s are still picked (async poll, not a single read).
  - No candidate appears within the bound → `WIDGET_TARGET_UNREACHABLE` naming the wait.
  - Two candidates in the same tier → `WIDGET_AMBIGUOUS_CHOICE` with both names in
    `details.offered`, and **no click was dispatched**.
  - A click that leaves the field's committed value unchanged → `WIDGET_NOT_COMMITTED`.
  - Driving an already-open listbox performs no opening click.

### TASK-003: Date drivers — calendar grid with weekday cross-check, and date inputs

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - `calendar-grid.ts`, in-page, returns for each visible day cell:
    `{ day, monthLabel, derivedDate, weekdayFromColumn, weekdayFromDate, disabled, selected, name, group }`.
    Date derivation order:
    1. machine-readable attributes — `data-date`, `data-day`, `datetime`, `value` — parsed as ISO
    2. the cell's `aria-label` parsed as a date via `Intl`-tolerant matching
    3. **structural**: the owning `<table>`/`[role="grid"]`'s month+year label (from `caption`,
       `thead th[colspan]`, the table's `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby`, or the nearest preceding
       heading in the panel), combined with the cell's day text
  - **Weekday cross-check** (the safety property): for structurally derived dates, compare the
    weekday implied by the cell's column index (from the grid's `<th>` weekday headers, honouring
    Sunday- vs Monday-first) against the weekday of the derived date. Any cell that disagrees is
    marked unsafe. If **any** cell in the target panel is unsafe, the driver returns
    `WIDGET_MAPPING_UNSAFE` with `details.derived` and `details.column` rather than clicking —
    a grid we cannot read consistently is one we must not act on.
  - `calendar-driver.ts` — `detect` scores on: the trigger's committed value parsing as a date or
    date range; `aria-haspopup` of `dialog`/`grid`; or a resolved container holding a
    `<table>`/`[role="grid"]` of day cells. `drive`:
    1. `openIfClosed`
    2. read the grid; if the target month is absent, page via a control named
       `Next`/`Previous` (month/year), requiring the month label to **change monotonically toward
       the target** each step, bounded by `maxPagingSteps` (12). A non-advancing or disabled
       control ends paging with `WIDGET_TARGET_UNREACHABLE` naming the months actually displayed.
    3. resolve the target cell's ref by `(name, group)` from a fresh `observe({ cap: 400 })`,
       falling back to `withTag`
    4. click; for `date_range`, re-read the grid and repeat for the end date (many pickers re-render
       or advance panels after the start pick)
    5. `readCommitted` + `matchesIntent`; mismatch → `WIDGET_NOT_COMMITTED` with the observed value
    6. `restore`
  - A disabled target cell is `WIDGET_TARGET_UNREACHABLE` with `details.reason: 'disabled'` — never
    a click.
  - `date-input-driver.ts` — `detect` returns 1.0 for `<input type="date">`, high for a text input
    whose `placeholder`/`pattern`/`aria-label` implies a date format. `drive` types the correctly
    formatted value, dispatches `input`+`change`, and verifies.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**:
  - jsdom two-panel fixture (August + September 2026, Aug 1 = Saturday, Sep 1 = Tuesday) with
    day cells carrying only bare numbers, matching the observed Expedia shape:
    - `{kind:'date', date:'2026-09-06'}` resolves to the **September** cell named `"6"`, not the
      August one. **This is the fault-C regression test.**
    - `{kind:'date_range', from:'2026-09-06', to:'2026-09-08'}` clicks exactly two cells, both in
      September, in that order.
  - A fixture whose day numbers are shifted one column relative to the weekday headers →
    `WIDGET_MAPPING_UNSAFE` and **zero clicks**. This is the safety property; assert it directly.
  - Cells carrying `data-date` attributes bypass structural derivation entirely (attributes win).
  - Monday-first and Sunday-first grids both derive correct weekdays.
  - Target three months ahead → paging advances exactly 3 steps and succeeds.
  - Paging control disabled before reaching the target → `WIDGET_TARGET_UNREACHABLE` listing the
    displayed months.
  - A paging control that does not change the month label → paging stops immediately, not after 12
    wasted clicks.
  - Disabled target cell → `WIDGET_TARGET_UNREACHABLE` with `reason: 'disabled'`, zero clicks.
  - Trigger value unchanged after clicking → `WIDGET_NOT_COMMITTED` with `details.committed`.
  - `<input type="date">` sets and verifies without opening anything.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: `docs/agent-tools.md` — the date-derivation order, the weekday
      cross-check and why it exists, and the paging bound. JSDoc on `calendar-grid.ts` covering all
      three derivation strategies.

### TASK-006: Rewire `browser_form_fill` onto the driver registry

- [ ] **Implementation**:

    Keep it accepted (a model that passes it must not get a schema error) and document it as
    deprecated.
  - Per field: resolve the target from the fresh uncapped observation, then
    `detectDriver(port, target)` with no family restriction.
    - A driver ≥ `MIN_CONFIDENCE` → build the intent from the field's `value` (ISO date → `date`;
      `<from>..<to>` or `<from>,<to>` → `date_range`; anything else → `option`) and `driveWidget`.
    - `WIDGET_NOT_RECOGNIZED` on a text-like role → plain `port.fill` (today's behavior).
    - `WIDGET_NOT_RECOGNIZED` on anything else → the existing `FORM_FIELD_UNSUPPORTED_ROLE`.

### TASK-007: Fix `computeGroup` ancestor fallthrough and panel-major ordering

- [ ] **Implementation**:
  - `interactable-scan.ts` `computeGroup`: move the `return null` out of the match branch so an
    ancestor that matches the selector but yields no label **continues the walk** instead of
    ending it. Return the first _non-empty_ label found within the depth bound; return `null` only
    when the walk completes with nothing. Raise the depth bound from 8 to 12 — Expedia's panel
    label sits above the inner `<table>`, which is what fault B exposed.
  - Add a heading fallback that also looks at the container's **preceding sibling** heading, not
    only descendants: many calendar panels render `<h2>August 2026</h2>` as a sibling of the grid.
  - `observe.ts`: make the ordering **panel-major** — within a scope, group elements by `group`
    (preserving first-appearance order of the groups by their minimum `top`, then `left`), and sort
    within each group by `(top, left)`. Ungrouped elements keep their current relative position.
    This is what actually de-interleaves side-by-side month panels (fault E); `(top, left)` alone
    cannot, because the panels genuinely share rows.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**:
  - jsdom: a day cell inside `<div aria-label="August 2026"><table><td role="button">6</td></table></div>`
    yields `group: 'August 2026'` — the direct fault-B regression test (the inner `<table>` matches
    first and must not terminate the walk).
  - A container whose label comes from a **preceding sibling** heading resolves.
  - A cell with no labelled ancestor within 12 levels yields `null`.
  - The nearest _labelled_ ancestor still wins over a farther one.
  - Ordering: a two-panel fixture yields all August cells contiguously before all September cells,
    despite shared `top` values.
  - Ungrouped page chrome retains its existing relative order.
  - `rankInteractables` and `DiscoveryObservation` validation are unaffected.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: JSDoc on `computeGroup` stating the continue-on-unlabelled rule and
      why. Update `buildAgentPageSnapshot`'s ordering contract in `docs/agent-tools.md`.
- **Verify**: `pnpm --filter @yantra/core test`. A live observation with the Expedia calendar open
  shows every day cell carrying `group: "August 2026"` or `"September 2026"`, panel-contiguous.

## 7. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: `browser_fill` with `secret_ref` remains the only credentialed path. Both new tools
  carry `browser_form_fill`'s `SECRET_SHAPE` guard and refuse credential-shaped values before any
  page interaction. Drivers never read `input[type=password]` values — FEAT-FP-009's in-page
  withholding rule is upstream of everything here. `assertHostBinding`, `withSecret`, and the
  consent flow are untouched.
- **Error Handling**: `WidgetErrorCode` is a closed union; every code carries `retryable` and a
  `details` payload naming the observed state (offered choices, displayed months, committed value).
  Every driver is bounded by `WidgetBudget` — `maxPagingSteps` 12, `maxActions` 24, plus an absolute
  deadline — so no driver can hang or loop. Both new tools are `mutating: true`, so the action-phase
  and confirmation middleware apply unchanged, and `trackFailureStreak` still keys on
  `${tool}:${errorCode}` for stuck-loop detection.
- **Logging**: No new log statements carry field values. Tool results reach `tool-calls.jsonl`
  having passed `maskUserInputDeep` → profile sanitizer → byte cap, as today. `details.offered`
  carries page-origin text and is therefore sanitized by the same path. The `withTag` fallback
  guarantees no `data-yantra-*` attribute survives a driver call, asserted by test.
- **Security**: Net posture is unchanged or stronger. The strict-verification rule removes a
  silent-wrong-value class (a click on a guessed cell reported as success). Page mutation is limited
  to a single temporary attribute with guaranteed cleanup, is not evasion, and does not touch the
  ethics/robots/rate-limit path. URL provenance is not relaxed further.
